self_description.text: ColliderBit Solo: an event-based LHC recast tool using the GAMBIT ColliderBit module.

caveat: Static read of the worktree and of the other pages' JSON. Nothing was built or run.

questions.title: What is the paper claiming CBS is?

evidence.fact: the only statement of purpose in the tree, and there is no second one
the runner itself is small: 10 files, +2,978 lines
the analysis work is not: 162 files, +11,073/−7,437, against a library of 137 registered names
the jet pipeline sits between them: 14 files, +1,098

and the subject is wider than this deck: ONNX (5 files), METSignificance (7 files) are absent from released GAMBIT entirely but predate the branch point, so they appear nowhere here — correct for a changelog, wrong for a paper

questions.title: Who is the reader, and how much GAMBIT do they already have?

evidence.fact: CBS asks for 2 dependencies but sits behind 69 declared backends — the gap only matters to reader two
123 retired analysis names only matter to reader one, who has YAML already written
the JSON contract, 8 top-level keys with 7 in-tree consumers, only matters to reader three
no file in the tree names a comparison framework or benchmarks against one
what CBS actually inherits and exposes is the ColliderBit likelihood machinery and a 137-analysis library — not event generation or detector simulation, which are Pythia’s and BuckFast’s
the histogram signal regions are the one mechanism with no obvious equivalent elsewhere: a binned distribution becoming per-bin likelihood terms

questions.title: Which check_histogram setting produced the published numbers?

evidence.fact: read with getValueOrDef, default false
2 of 3 histogram analyses run in signal-region mode, contributing 23 extra signal regions when the flag is on
only 2 of 9 histogram macros guard themselves (FILL_HISTOGRAM_1D, FILL_HISTOGRAM_2D); the rest rely on the caller checking

questions.title: Are variable-R jets smeared, and is that the intended physics?

evidence.fact: jetcollections_no_smear declared on the smearing object
2 continue sites drop those collections out of the smearing loop
the list is filled from the VR settings at 3 wiring sites, so membership is automatic — a collection is excluded by being variable-R, not by anyone choosing to exclude it
2 analyses consume VR jets and inherit the choice: ATLAS_EXOT_2019_04, ATLAS_EXOT_2019_07

questions.title: Which of the twelve new analyses are validated, and against what?

evidence.fact: no cutflow instrumentation: ATLAS_EXOT_2016_013, ATLAS_EXOT_2018_60, ATLAS_EXOT_2019_04, ATLAS_EXOT_2021_35, CMS_SUS_16_039
ATLAS_EXOT_2018_60 — “TODO: Implement the published selection and signal-region yields.”
ATLAS_SUSY_2018_07 — “Not validated, still in progress”
CMS_B2G_18_003 — “vectors are still TODO (their histograms commit no SRs until the data are supplied, but”
ATLAS_EXOT_2018_60 is tracked as skeleton — run() carries a TODO; collect_results() is empty. Registered only.
CMS_B2G_18_003 is tracked as partial — 3M histogram SRs digitised; 3T/2M1L obs/bkg pending; high-mass is a cut-and-count approximation, not the CMS shape fit.

questions.title: Ship the default cards, and make a run self-describing

evidence.fact: CBS_yaml/CBS_defaults.yaml, 22 lines of settings, currently ignored by git — a packaging step, not a question
absent defaults return silently rather than failing, so the run proceeds on whatever the compiled-in values happen to be

questions.title: What does the configuration section actually document?

evidence.fact: min_nEvents forced to (long long)(1000)
max_nEvents forced to (long long)(std::numeric_limits<int>::max())
run_convergence_checks forced to false — CBS policy: always process all events provided by the user (no convergence-based early stop).
of the 14 keys in the original example file, only 3 are still genuinely the user’s to set — 7 are defaulted by the program, 1 is conditional, and 3 are read by nothing

evidence.fact: 123 names retired, 132 introduced, 128 → 137 registered overall
80 renames documented across 75 git-detected file moves, including 18 consolidations absorbing 56 files

7 in-tree consumers already parse it, with their own guards for fields they expect
